spec: Build an expense-tracking API. Users record expenses with an amount, category and date, list expenses filtered by category or month, and request a summary endpoint that returns total spend per category for a given month. Expenses are stored in DynamoDB.

complexity.rationale: One store, but compound filtering and monthly aggregation make it more than basic CRUD.

congruence_checklist: GET endpoint filtering by category and month
Summary endpoint aggregating spend per category
Expense model has amount, category, date

plan.summary: A JSON REST API for personal expense tracking. Clients (a web/mobile front-end or scripts) create expense records consisting of an amount, category and date, retrieve individual expenses, list expenses filtered by category and/or calendar month, update or delete them, and request a per-category spend summary for a given month. All records persist in a single DynamoDB table; aggregation for the summary endpoint is computed in the service from the queried items. The service is a standalone FastAPI process that talks to DynamoDB directly with boto3 — no asynchronous, scheduled or event-driven work is implied by the specification, so no queues, topics or Lambda functions are planned.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness/readiness probe used by the evaluation harness; verifies the process is up and the DynamoDB table is reachable.
Record a new expense from a JSON body containing amount, category, date and optional description/user_id; generates an expense_id and writes the item to DynamoDB.
List expenses for a user, optionally filtered by ?category= and/or ?month=YYYY-MM, with optional limit/pagination cursor.
Fetch a single expense record by its identifier.
Update the amount, category, date or description of an existing expense.
Delete an expense record by its identifier.
Return total spend per category for a required ?month=YYYY-MM query parameter, plus the overall total and expense count for that month.

data_models.name: Expense
fields: user_id: string (owner partition key, defaults to 'default')
amount: decimal (positive, 2dp, stored as DynamoDB Number)
month: string (derived YYYY-MM bucket used as a GSI partition key)

aws_resources.name: expenses
aws_resources.justification: Primary persistence for expense records as the spec explicitly requires DynamoDB storage. Partition key user_id (string), sort key expense_id (string), PAY_PER_REQUEST billing; serves POST /expenses writes and GET /expenses/{id} reads.

aws_resources.name: expenses.month-date-index (GSI)
aws_resources.justification: Global secondary index with partition key month (YYYY-MM) and sort key date so GET /expenses?month= and GET /expenses/summary can query one month's items directly instead of scanning the table.

aws_resources.name: expenses.category-date-index (GSI)
aws_resources.justification: Global secondary index with partition key category and sort key date so GET /expenses?category= filtering is a query; month filtering is applied as a key-condition/filter on the date sort key when both filters are supplied.

aws_resources.name: expense-tracker-app-policy-and-role
aws_resources.justification: Least-privilege policy granting the backend service credentials GetItem/PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem/Query on the expenses table and Query on its two GSIs, plus CloudWatch Logs write permissions. Attached to a role the standalone service assumes.

aws_resources.name: /cloudforge/expense-tracker-api (log group)
aws_resources.justification: Destination for the API's structured application logs (request traces, validation failures, DynamoDB errors) written by the running service; provides retention configuration and operational visibility.

events: 🧭 Parsed specification → expense_tracker_api (fastapi); AWS resources: DynamoDB:expenses, DynamoDB:expenses.month-date-index (GSI), DynamoDB:expenses.category-date-index (GSI), IAM:expense-tracker-app-policy-and-role, CloudWatch:/cloudforge/expense-tracker-api (log group)

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 6 files — FastAPI expense-tracking service split into a thin HTTP layer (app.py) and a boto3/DynamoDB repository (storage.py) behind an injectable `ExpenseRepository` interface. Endpoints: GET /health, POST /expenses, GET /expenses (category/month/limit/cursor filters), GET /expenses/summary (declared before the path-param route), GET/PUT/DELETE /expenses/{expense_id}. DynamoDB access uses AWS_ENDPOINT_URL and us-east-1 defaults, table/index names from env (expenses, month-date-index, category-date-index), Decimal-safe amounts, base64 pagination cursors, conditional updates mapped to 404, and storage failures mapped to 503. tests/test_app.py exercises every endpoint with FastAPI TestClient plus an in-memory fake repo, and unit-tests the storage layer with monkeypatched boto3/fake tables — no network or LocalStack required. Requirements limited to fastapi, uvicorn, boto3, pydantic.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform for the expense_tracker_api plan, split across versions.tf, variables.tf, main.tf and outputs.tf.

Resources (each traced to the plan's aws_resources list):
- aws_dynamodb_table.expenses — PAY_PER_REQUEST, hash key user_id / range key expense_id, with the two planned GSIs (month-date-index: month+date, category-date-index: category+date, both ALL projection). Point-in-time recovery enabled and server-side encryption with a customer managed KMS key (satisfies CKV_AWS_28 / CKV_AWS_119).
- aws_cloudwatch_log_group.app — /cloudforge/expense-tracker-api with 365-day retention and KMS encryption (CKV_AWS_66 / CKV_AWS_158).
- aws_iam_role.app + aws_iam_policy.app + attachment — least privilege: item-level DynamoDB actions scoped to the table ARN, Query scoped to the two index ARNs, log stream/put events scoped to the log group ARN, and KMS usage scoped to the single key ARN. No "*" actions or "*" resources; the trust policy names explicit service principals rather than a wildcard.
- aws_kms_key.main + alias — the supporting CMK required by the DynamoDB and CloudWatch encryption checks; key rotation enabled, key policy grants account root administration plus scoped CloudWatch Logs / DynamoDB usage (no wildcard principals).

No S3, SQS, SNS, Lambda or API Gateway resources were generated because the plan's service is a standalone FastAPI process with no event-driven work. Only LocalStack Community services (DynamoDB, IAM, CloudWatch Logs, KMS) are used. The provider sets default_tags with project, managed-by and environment, and hashicorp/aws is pinned to ~> 5.0.
